---

An exercise is a playground with an `exercise` ID, plus any number of hints,
an optional solution, and an optional check, all tied to it by that ID. They
follow the same `exercise="..."` convention as
[Quarto Live](https://r-wasm.github.io/quarto-live/).

## A complete exercise

Here is a small exercise, followed by its source.

**Give this document a subtitle, and make the word "quickly" bold.**

````{quarto-simulator}
#| exercise: ex-demo
#| height: 300
---
title: "Release notes"
---

We fixed the bug quickly.
````

::: {.hint exercise="ex-demo"}
A subtitle is set in the YAML header, like the title: `subtitle: "..."`.
:::

::: {.hint exercise="ex-demo"}
In markdown, `**two asterisks**` on each side make text bold.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex-demo"}
```markdown
---
title: "Release notes"
subtitle: "Version 2.0"
---

We fixed the bug **quickly**.
```
:::

```{quarto-simulator-check}
#| exercise: ex-demo
if (!result.yaml.subtitle) return fail("There's no subtitle yet. Add `subtitle:` to the YAML header.")
const bold = [...result.html.querySelectorAll("main strong")].map(el => el.textContent)
if (!bold.includes("quickly")) return fail("Make the word `quickly` bold with `**quickly**`.")
return pass("The document has a subtitle and a bold word.")
```

The source of that exercise:

`````markdown
````{quarto-simulator}
#| exercise: ex-demo
---
title: "Release notes"
---

We fixed the bug quickly.
````

::: {.hint exercise="ex-demo"}

:::

::: {.hint exercise="ex-demo"}
In markdown, `**two asterisks**` on each side make text bold.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex-demo"}
```markdown

```
:::

```{quarto-simulator-check}

if (!result.yaml.subtitle) return fail("There's no subtitle yet. Add `subtitle:` to the YAML header.")
const bold = [...result.html.querySelectorAll("main strong")].map(el => el.textContent)
if (!bold.includes("quickly")) return fail("Make the word `quickly` bold with `**quickly**`.")
return pass("The document has a subtitle and a bold word.")
```
`````

## Hints

`::: {.hint exercise="ID"}` divs are hidden until the learner presses
**💡 Hint**. Each press reveals the next hint, in order, so start general and
get more specific. Hints are ordinary markdown.

## Solutions

A `::: {.solution exercise="ID"}` div is revealed by **Show solution**. If it
contains a code block, the learner also gets a **Copy solution into the
editor** button, which replaces their document with the block's content. Use
a `markdown` code block holding the whole document, as above. If the
solution document has code cells, use a longer fence for the outer block:

`````markdown
::: {.solution exercise="ex-plot"}
````markdown
---
title: "Plot"
---

```{r}
#| echo: false
plot(cars)
```
````
:::
`````

## Checks

A `quarto-simulator-check` block holds the body of an async JavaScript
function. **✓ Check** renders the learner's document, then runs it. It must
return `pass(message)` or `fail(message)`. Messages are short markdown:
backticks show as code.

If the document fails to render, the check fails without running and points
the learner to the error, so checks only ever see documents that rendered.

The function receives `result`:

| Field      | Contents                                                                      |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `source`   | The learner's full text                                                       |
| `yaml`     | The parsed front matter, as an object                                         |
| `body`     | Everything after the front matter                                             |
| `html`     | The rendered preview as a `Document`, so `querySelector` works                |
| `text`     | The rendered preview as plain text                                            |
| `cells`    | `[{ lang, code, options, outputs: [{ type, text }] }]`, one per code cell      |
| `warnings` | Render warnings, such as unresolved cross-references                          |

Output types are `stdout`, `stderr`, `error` and `plot`, and for Python also
`result` (the value of the cell's last line) and `display` (`display()` and
rich output such as pandas tables).

### Patterns

Check one requirement at a time, in the order the instructions list them, and
say what to do next. The first failing requirement is the one the learner
sees.

**YAML options.** `result.yaml` holds what the learner wrote, so the check
sees exactly where an option is:

```js
if (result.yaml.toc !== true) return fail("Turn on a table of contents with `toc: true`.")
if (result.yaml.format?.html?.["code-fold"] !== true) {
  return fail("`code-fold` is an option of the `html` format. Put it under `format: html:`.")
}
```

**What rendered.** `result.html` is the page the learner sees, so checks can
test the result rather than the spelling:

```js
const tip = result.html.querySelector(".callout-tip")
if (!tip) return fail("Add a tip callout: `::: {.callout-tip}`.")
if (!result.html.querySelector("nav#TOC")) return fail("The table of contents isn't showing yet.")
if (!result.html.querySelector("a.quarto-xref")) return fail("Refer to the figure with `@fig-...`.")
```

**Code cells.** `result.cells` has each cell's options, after the document's
`execute` defaults are applied, and its outputs:

```js
const cell = result.cells.find(c => c.lang === "r")
if (!cell) return fail("The R code cell is missing.")
if (cell.options.echo !== false) return fail("Hide the code with `#| echo: false`.")
if (!cell.outputs.some(o => o.type === "plot")) return fail("The cell should draw a plot.")
```

**Warnings.** A broken cross-reference renders as `?@fig-name` and appears
in `result.warnings`:

```js
if (result.warnings.some(w => w.includes("Unable to resolve crossref"))) {
  return fail("A cross-reference doesn't match any label. Check the spelling after `@`.")
}
```

Checks run in the learner's browser, so a determined learner can read them.
They are feedback, not an exam.
